summary: Hermann Kulke is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of Freiburg (~1962–1967). He held the Chair of Asian History at the University of Kiel (1988) and an attested post at Heidelberg University (2004).

Hermann Oldenberg (1854–1920) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1871–1875). He held professorships at Berlin (~1878–1889), the University of Kiel (~1889–1908), and the University of Göttingen (~1908–1920).

Hermann Osthoff (1847–1909) worked in linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1875–1877) and Heidelberg University (~1877–1909), and founded the publication Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen.
Hermann Sauppe (1809–1893) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1838–1845) and the University of Göttingen (~1856–1893).

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel (1820–1875) was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1836–1838) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1838–1842) under August Friedrich Pott. He later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1872–1875).

Hermann von Schlagintweit (1826–1882) worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1846–1849) and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1852–1854).
Hideaki Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University, where he also held a post as a researcher (attested 1995).

Hideaki Nakatani is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (1966) under Gadjin Nagao, under Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He was a professor at Kobe Gakuin University (attested 2003).
Hidehiko Kurita works in religious studies and Japanology. He completed a PhD at Tohoku University and served as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University (attested 2020).
Hideki Kiyoshima is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Delhi and held an attested post as a lecturer at Kindai University (1989).
Hidenaka Tanaka (1886–1974) worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909) and held a post at Kyoto Women's University (~1948–1957).

Hidenori S. Sakuma specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying at the University of Tokyo and earning a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. Sakuma held posts at Shitennoji University, Taisho University, and the University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima (1927–2013) was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He held professorships at Waseda University (~1968–1998, attested 1999), Bunkyo Gakuin University, and Sanko Research Institute (attested 2008).
Hideo Sakurai (1916–2011) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University until 1943. He later served as professor emeritus at Komazawa University (attested 1982–1992).

Hideomi Yaita is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University. He served as a research assistant at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1985) and as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Hideto Ono works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Hidetoshi Yoshizawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held positions at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998–2008) and as a chief research fellow (attested 2017).

Hideyo Ogawa is an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Hiroshima University (~1974–1982). Ogawa continued at Hiroshima University as an assistant professor (~1987–1996) and as Professor of Indian Philosophy (~1996–2019).
Hideyuki Matsumori is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied as a doctoral student at Soka University (attested 2006) and later held an assistant professor post there (attested 2015).
Hildegard Diemberger specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She conducted work supervised by Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner.
